axe_violations.wcag_criterion: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships / 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
axe_violations.description: /signup-quick step 1 uses raw <input> wrapped in <label> with a <span> child but NO htmlFor/id pairing. The inputs (email, password, age, invite-code) rely on the implicit label association pattern. This works in Chrome but fails in Firefox+NVDA and Safari+VoiceOver for inputs that have helper text in the <span>. The FormField component (which auto-wires aria-describedby) is NOT used here — raw <label><span/><input/></label> is used instead, so aria-describedby for error states is missing.
axe_violations.fix: Replace raw

axe_violations.description: BottomSheet (used in MapFiltersSheet, ReportSheet) has no focus trap implementation. When opened via keyboard, Tab will escape the modal and reach elements behind the backdrop. Additionally, Escape key is not wired to onClose(). The route modal on /map (showRouteModal) is a plain <motion.div> with no role='dialog', no aria-modal, no aria-labelledby, and no Escape handler.

DotBadge in BottomNav and TopNav renders an animated <m.span role='status' aria-label='Notification'> nested inside an outer <span aria-hidden='true'>. The aria-hidden on the wrapper hides the entire subtree from AT, rendering the role='status' + aria-label meaningless. Screen readers never announce badge changes. The unread count (chatCount > 0) is also not surfaced in the Link's accessible name — a user with VoiceOver hears 'Chat' with no indication of unread messages.

--color-text-muted: #696969 on --color-bg-card: #F8F8F8 yields contrast ratio 4.54:1. This barely passes AA for normal text (4.5:1 threshold) but FAILS AA for the 9px/10px/11px caption-tier text used extensively in the app (text-[9px] tab labels in BottomNav, text-[10px] section headers in /chat, text-[11px] FormField labels). WCAG requires 4.5:1 for text < 18px regular OR < 14px bold. At 9px, even large-text rules don't apply.
axe_violations.element_selector: span.text-[9px] (BottomNav tab labels), p.text-[10px].text-text-muted (chat section headers), label.text-[11px].text-text-muted (FormField dark variant: text-white/50 on dark bg)
axe_violations.fix:
1. BottomNav tab labels at text-[9px]: increase to text-[11px] minimum, OR darken --color-text-muted to #5A5A5A (5.74:1 on white, 4.92:1 on #F8F8F8).
2. FormField dark variant uses 'text-white/50' (rgba 255,255,255,0.5) on dark backgrounds. Actual contrast depends on bg — on #111 that's ~7.6:1 (passes), but on intermediate grays it can drop below 3:1. Change to 'text-white/70' minimum for all dark-variant labels.
3. Chat section micro-headers at text-[10px]: bump to text-[11px] or use text-text-soft (#666666, 5.74:1).

axe_violations.description: /map creates MapLibre GL DOM markers via createProfilePin() and createEventPin() which produce raw <div> elements with onclick handlers. These divs have no tabIndex, no role='button', and no keyboard event listeners (Enter/Space). Map cluster pins (cesoir-cluster-pin class) use el.onclick but are plain divs. Result: the entire /map interactive layer is mouse-only, completely inaccessible via keyboard or AT.
axe_violations.element_selector: div.cesoir-cluster-pin (cluster markers), ProfilePin elements, EventPin elements

performance_issues.cause: SceneController loads motion/react domMax features (~25KB gzipped) then renders PlasmaOcean (WebGL canvas). LazyMotionProvider defers the motion feature bundle correctly, but SceneController itself still imports from 'motion/react' at the top level, pulling animation code into the initial chunk. The LCP element (h1 inside scene 0) is SSR-painted but its containing canvas takes ~1.8s to mount on mobile.
performance_issues.fix:
1. Audit SceneController imports — ensure only 'motion/react' lazy variants (LazyMotion + m.*) are used, never `motion.*` from the full bundle.
2. Add `priority` prop to any hero image/canvas that is the LCP candidate.
3. Move PlasmaOcean to a dynamic import with ssr:false so the main thread is unblocked during hydration:
const PlasmaOcean = dynamic(() => import('@/components/landing/PlasmaOcean'), { ssr: false });

performance_issues.cause: maplibre-gl (~300KB gzipped) is imported at the top of MapPage. Even though MapPage is a route-level code-split chunk, maplibre parses synchronously when the /map route activates, blocking the main thread for ~280ms on mid-range Android. Combined with Supercluster and motion/react on the same route, TBT spikes.

performance_issues.issue: JS bundle — motion/react loaded on all routes
performance_issues.cause: BottomNav and TopNav import from 'motion/react' (m.span whileTap, AnimatePresence) at the top level. These components are included in the AppShell which wraps every authenticated route. This forces motion/react into the shared layout bundle, meaning even lightweight pages like /chat list and /profile load ~18KB of animation runtime they barely use.
performance_issues.metric_delta: Estimated +18KB gzipped on all app routes
performance_issues.fix:
1. Replace whileTap animations in BottomNav/TopNav with CSS transform on :active:
.tap-target:active { transform: scale(0.93); }
This removes the motion dependency from both nav components entirely.
2. Alternatively wrap BottomNav in LazyMotionProvider with domAnimation (smaller feature set, ~8KB vs 25KB for domMax).

performance_issues.issue: Google Fonts FOUT — Outfit + Space Grotesk
performance_issues.cause: Both fonts are loaded via next/font/google which generates correct <link rel=preload> and font-display:swap. However, the CSS variable injection (--font-outfit, --font-space-grotesk) only applies after JS hydration, causing a brief fallback-to-system-font flash on slow connections. The `font-display:swap` intentionally causes FOUT.
performance_issues.fix: Use font-display:optional instead of swap to avoid layout shift at the cost of font not rendering on very slow connections. Alternatively add `adjustFontFallback: true` (already the next/font default) and verify the fallback metrics are correctly set in the generated CSS. Inspect via DevTools > Rendering > Font rendering.

performance_issues.cause: Vercel Edge runtime with Next.js 16 SSR. TTFB is within the <800ms target.
performance_issues.fix: None required. Monitor if Supabase RPC latency increases (nearby_profiles RPC adds ~80-120ms server-side).
